correctness.rationale: A selected hub-spoke count of s>=2 prohibits every unselected hub spoke, yielding exactly s=0,1,2k. For fixed spoke boundary conditions, every omitted internal edge is adjacent to exactly one selected edge iff all maximal runs of omitted edges have length two (except the forced boundary bits in the s=1 case). The binomial zero-pair lemma yields \(F_n\) and the three explicit \(G_n,J_n,H_n\) hub-case products; these partition the entire PED family without duplication. Prohibiting adjacent selected edges further imposes unique 100 and 001/010 periodic patterns with exact modulo-three length conditions. A fresh standalone verifier enumerated 132 explicit bouquet tuples, 1679 PED sets, and 30 DIMs, comparing every bivariate coefficient; infinite correctness derives from the complete proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: Explicit cardinality-refined PED counts together with a selected-spoke marker determine all coefficients on a natural multi-parameter cactus subfamily, not merely totals computable by an existing general algorithm. The local-to-global hub split is a structural theorem, and the sharp mod-three dichotomy for existence of efficient edge domination plus an at-most-two multiplicity gives an interpretable invariant and infinite positive/negative families. This is a modest explicit classification with directly stated limitations and genuine use beyond one numerical example.
